title: Beyond urban form: Introducing dynamic factors in agent-based simulations of pedestrian movement
abstract: While research on route choice behaviour in cities has focused extensively on the role of urban form, including street configuration and meaningful urban elements, in shaping pedestrians’ decisions, less attention has been given to the role of dynamic factors. These are phenomena arising from social (e.g. crowding and noise) and natural environments (e.g. weather conditions) that vary across space and time. Agent-Based Models (ABMs) of pedestrian movement, simulation tools that allow researchers to observe the emergence of macro-level patterns (e.g. pedestrian flows) from micro-level mechanisms, have been widely influenced by research on static urban elements. However, dynamic factors remain underrepresented in such modelling frameworks. The aim of this paper is to incorporate the effects of crowding and noise on route choice behaviour into an empirically grounded and evaluated ABM of pedestrian movement. In the ABM, route choice behaviour is conceptualised as emerging from the interplay between individual preferences and environmental attractors and repellers previously identified in empirical work. Poznań (Poland) was selected as the study area. First, we conducted a Sensitivity Analysis (SA) to assess the impact of specific model inputs on both micro-level (characteristics of individual routes) and macro-level (agent volumes across the street network) outputs. Then, based on individual behavioural differences identified in the empirical study and the results of the SA, we parametrised the ABM and derived five agent types, each characterised by a distinct set of preferences. Lastly, we assessed the incorporation of crowding and noise into the agent behavioural mechanisms to evaluate the extent to which these dynamic factors shaped the ABM results. The analysis revealed that both urban form and dynamic factors influence pedestrian route choice in complex, non-linear ways, with several interaction effects. Although urban form played an important role in shaping pedestrian routes, dynamic factors also affected route choice: they reduced route length and spatial dispersion, leading agents to concentrate across a narrower set of street segments. Furthermore, we found significant differences in the movement patterns generated by the different agent types. Finally, we observed that agents often traversed green spaces, squares, and other relatively open routes to alleviate the sense of overcrowding in busier parts of the network.
abstractZh: 城市路径选择行为研究广泛关注街道构型及有意义的城市要素等城市形态对行人决策的影响，而对动态因素的关注相对不足。这些因素包括随时空变化的社会环境现象（如拥挤、噪声）与自然环境现象（如天气）。行人移动的基于智能体模型（ABM）允许研究者观察微观机制如何涌现为行人流等宏观模式，现有模型深受静态城市要素研究影响，动态因素在其中仍体现不足。本文旨在将拥挤和噪声对路径选择的影响纳入具有实证基础并经过评估的行人移动ABM。模型将路径选择视为个体偏好与实证研究所识别的环境吸引因素和排斥因素相互作用的结果。研究区域为波兰波兹南。首先，通过敏感性分析评估特定模型输入对微观输出（个体路径特征）和宏观输出（街道网络智能体数量）的影响。随后，依据实证识别的个体行为差异及敏感性分析结果设定模型参数，形成五类偏好不同的智能体。最后，评估将拥挤和噪声纳入行为机制后，这些动态因素在多大程度上改变模型结果。分析表明，城市形态与动态因素以复杂、非线性的方式影响行人路径选择，并存在多种交互效应。城市形态对行人路径具有重要作用，动态因素同样影响路径选择：它们缩短路径长度、降低空间分散程度，使智能体集中于更有限的街段。不同智能体类型生成的移动模式也存在显著差异。此外，智能体经常穿行绿地、广场及其他较开阔路径，以缓解网络繁忙区域带来的过度拥挤感。
